Hmm, that seems backwards but let's just take columns at face value: col1 = 6000, 345 Ω, 440 Ω, 0.67 μV, 4-wire; col2 = 3000, 85 Ω, 3300 Ω, 1 μV, 6-wire.

Hmm wait, actually think: with 4-wire (no sense lines) the voltage drop across the cable matters, so longer cable (max 3 m) and higher impedance (345–440 Ω, typical 350 Ω cells) works. With 6-wire with sense lines, you can drive lower impedance cells down to 85 Ω and up to 3300 Ω, cable unlimited length, but fewer scale intervals (3000) because excitation voltage regulation? Actually 6-wire with remote sense should be better... Whatever — take as given.
